steps.body: Direct: $12$. Single indirect: $1024$. Double indirect: $1024^2 = 2^{20}$. Total $= 12 + 1024 + 1048576 = 1049612$ blocks.

steps.title: Size
steps.body: $1049612 \times 4\,\text{KB} = 48\,\text{KB} + 4\,\text{MB} + 4\,\text{GB} \approx 4.0039\,\text{GB} \approx \mathbf{4.0}$ GB.

pitfalls: Using 32-bit addresses as a 4 GB cap on *disk* rather than counting blocks — the answer is still ≈ 4.0 GB here.
cse-2019-cs-42.verification: Dominant term $2^{20} \times 2^{12} = 2^{32}$ B = 4 GB; the rest adds only ≈ 4 MB.

cse-2019-cs-43.approach: Advance the dot over $\langle$ in the only item of $I_0$ that has $\bullet\langle$, then take the closure (add items for $L$, then for $S$).

steps.title: Items of I₀
steps.body: $I_0 = \{ S' \to \bullet S,\; S \to \bullet\langle L\rangle,\; S \to \bullet id \}$.

steps.title: Kernel of GOTO(I₀, ⟨)
steps.body: Only $S \to \bullet\langle L \rangle$ moves: kernel $S \to \langle \bullet L \rangle$.

steps.title: Closure
steps.body:
Dot before $L$: add $L \to \bullet L,S$ and $L \to \bullet S$. Dot before $S$: add $S \to \bullet\langle L\rangle$ and $S \to \bullet id$.

Items: $S \to \langle\bullet L\rangle$, $L \to \bullet L,S$, $L \to \bullet S$, $S \to \bullet\langle L\rangle$, $S \to \bullet id$ → **5**.

pitfalls: Stopping after the $L$-items and forgetting to close over $S$.
cse-2019-cs-43.verification: Every non-terminal after a dot (L, S) has all its productions included; no duplicates.

cse-2019-cs-48.approach: The DFA only needs to track the current product $\pi$ of the prefix, an element of the permutation group $S_5$. All $5! = 120$ products are reachable and pairwise distinguishable, so the minimum DFA has 120 states.

steps.title: Upper bound
steps.body: States = permutations of $\{1..5\}$; start and accepting state = $id$; on symbol $\sigma$ go from $g$ to $g\circ\sigma$. That DFA has $5! = 120$ states and accepts $L$.

steps.title: All states needed
steps.body: Each permutation is a one-letter string, so all 120 states are reachable. For prefixes $x, y$ with $\pi(x) = g \ne h = \pi(y)$, append the single symbol $g^{-1}$: $\pi(xg^{-1}) = id$ but $\pi(yg^{-1}) = hg^{-1} \ne id$. So they are distinguishable.

steps.title: Answer
steps.body: No dead state is needed (every element has an inverse), so the minimum is **120**.

pitfalls: Adding a dead state — it would never be reached, because any product can be brought back to $id$.
cse-2019-cs-48.verification: $|S_5| = 5! = 120$, and Myhill–Nerode classes correspond one-to-one with group elements.

cse-2019-cs-50.approach: Simplify with a K-map: the minterms give $f = BD + \bar B\bar D = B \odot D$ (XNOR). Write it as a product of sums, which maps directly to a two-level NOR–NOR circuit.

steps.title: Simplify
steps.body: With $f(A,B,C,D)$: minterms $0,2,8,10$ have $B = 0, D = 0$ → $\bar B\bar D$; minterms $5,7,13,15$ have $B = 1, D = 1$ → $BD$. So $f = BD + \bar B\bar D$.

steps.title: POS form
steps.body: $f = (\bar B + D)(B + \bar D)$ (check: expanding gives $\bar B B + \bar B\bar D + BD + D\bar D = BD + \bar B\bar D$).

steps.title: NOR–NOR
steps.body: $f = \text{NOR}\big(\text{NOR}(\bar B, D),\ \text{NOR}(B, \bar D)\big)$, since $\overline{\overline{(x+y)} + \overline{(u+v)}} = (x+y)(u+v)$. Complements are available, so **3** gates. One or two NOR gates realise only single sums or a product of one sum with literals, not XNOR.
